messages:
customer_acme: Hey team — after the model bump last week our customer-facing assistant started replying much more tersely. Nothing broken but tone shifted; fewer polite sign-offs and shorter explanations. Happening across multiple prompts. Not urgent crash-y but it's causing support tickets. Example below.

customer_acme: Prompt they sent: 
```
User: How can I reset my password?
```

customer_acme: Response (expected / before pin to older model):
```
Assistant: Hi! To reset your password, go to Settings → Account → Reset password, enter your email, and follow the reset link we send. If you don't receive the email, check spam or reach out to support@acme.com and we'll help. Have a great day!
```

customer_acme: Response (observed after upgrade to redwood-small-2.4.0):
```
Assistant: Go to Settings → Account → Reset password and follow the link.
```

jess_support: Thanks for the clear repro, this helps. Can you paste the API request_id or response headers for one call? Also which deployment/region are you on and when did you first see it?

customer_acme: request_id: req_6b3f2a, region: us-west-2, first seen right after the deploy on 2026-03-12 ~11:15 PDT. We didn't change any client params; temperature still 0.2.

jess_support: Got it — I'm escalating. @sam_engineer can you grab the service logs for req_6b3f2a and confirm the model/version that served it? Also confirm if any system prompt or safety layer changes were rolled out.

sam_engineer: Looking now. ops-bot show-deploy req_6b3f2a

ops-bot: deploy-log: deployment_id=dep-44a9, model=redwood-small-2.4.0, runtime=prod, rollout=2026-03-12T18:05Z, canary=false, config={"temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":256} 

sam_engineer: Confirmed model redwood-small-2.4.0 served that request. No customer-side overrides.

mike_prod: Thx. We shipped a micro-change in the system prompt (brevity bias) to reduce token usage in some reply categories. It was intended to only affect low-tier assistant responses but might have been applied more broadly. @anya_ml can you check model behaviour deltas?

anya_ml: I'm running a rapid A/B: 1000 prompts sample across support-style queries comparing v2.3.9 -> v2.4.0. Early signal shows a statistically significant drop in average response length (~22% fewer tokens) and reduction in sign-off phrases. Also seeing slightly higher probability mass on shorter completions (EOS token earlier). Could be system prompt or change to decoding fastpath that favors brevity.

anya_ml: Can you share a small set of representative prompts (we need diversity: how-to, policy, empathetic responses)? I want to reproduce locally with pinned seed and sampling params.

customer_acme: Sure, here's a short set we use in tests: 
```
- "How do I cancel my subscription?"
- "My invoice is wrong, what do I do?"
- "I forgot my password and can't login."
- "The charge on my card is unfamiliar, help."
```

jess_support: Also capture your full SDK call (headers). Some customers inadvertently send different model param overrides when upgrading client libs.

customer_acme: Our calls are standard; no model param overrides. We tested pinning the model to redwood-small-2.3.9 and the tone went back to normal immediately — same inputs produced longer, slightly more apologetic replies.

anya_ml: That confirms a regression introduced between 2.3.9 -> 2.4.0. Next steps I'm running:
- deterministic replays with same RNG seed and sampling params on both versions
- log-prob analysis to see where EOS probability spikes
- check system prompt diff and any tokenization/decoder changes

mike_prod: If it's the system prompt change we pushed, we should consider a targeted rollback on the assistant-tier routing while we investigate. Sam, can you scope an emergency pin for acme to 2.3.9?

sam_engineer: I can pin the tenant to 2.3.9 for now; will open a customer-facing rollback and note in the console. Doing it now.

ops-bot: tenant-pin: tenant=acme, from_model=redwood-small-2.4.0, to_model=redwood-small-2.3.9, change_id=chg-9921, started=2026-03-13T02:30Z

customer_acme: Confirmed — after pinning responses look like before. Thanks. We're OK with pin while you investigate.

anya_ml: Interim quick findings: system prompt diff shows an added sentence aimed at brevity. Also a small change in the sample weighting for the fastpath decoder that slightly favors shorter outputs. Both together explain the effect. I'll prepare a mitigation PR to revert brevity-injection and adjust decoder weighting.

mike_prod: Sounds like a plan. Can you add an eval metric to prevent future accidental brevity shifts (e.g., median tokens per reply for support prompts + sign-off presence)? Also add a release-note checklist item: "run tone/verbosity regression suite".

anya_ml: Adding eval and gating checks. I'll post the A/B report here when ready.

jess_support: Thanks everyone. Customer is pinned and happy. I'll update the ticket and follow-up with a postmortem summary once we have the root cause and the fix deployed. @customer_acme we'll keep you updated — sorry for the disruption. :pray:

customer_acme: Appreciate the quick action. Hoping the fix lands soon — thank you! :thumbsup:
